summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of diabetes, kidney transplant, and a left upper extremity arteriovenous graft presented with a non-healing ulcer on his left index finger and nocturnal hand pain. Evaluation revealed no acute osteomyelitis on imaging, but clinical concern for vascular steal syndrome from the unused AV graft led to surgical ligation. The procedure was performed successfully without complications. During admission, the patient experienced hyperglycemia and hypertension, prompting insulin regimen adjustment and initiation of eplerenone for suspected hyperaldosteronism. He remained stable, afebrile, and pain-controlled, tolerating oral intake and ambulating independently. He was discharged home with instructions to continue transplant and diabetic medications, wound care, and follow-up with vascular surgery, transplant clinic, and plastic surgery for ongoing monitoring.
